The proof uses only complement symmetry and minimality, and it covers 33,556 of the 58,875 crossing knots tested.

results.title: Every pinning on a plane side has access, and none does on the non-planar census spaces
results.statement: Re-centring the potentials at any point keeps them convex, so on a plane side every pinning pair reaches the ports and every crossing knot pinned by two near points is generated, while on the Fano plane and census 58 no pinning by two non-port points has access. The premise then rests on 12,102 residual knots, all generated on every splice tested but without a proof.

results.title: A removal orients the tree of cuts, and held cuts compose as iterated 2-sums
results.statement: Removing a line holds every cut pointing toward it and opens every cut pointing away; beyond a held cut nothing depends on the removal. The knots crossing only held cuts are exactly the iterated 2-sums, through held hubs, of knots crossing no cut, so new emergence lives only across opened cuts.

results.title: Opened cuts form one zone of emergence that hubs do not localize
results.statement: Opened cuts do not act separately: new knots of one are carried across others, and two or three create knots of three or four points jointly. On 96 chains of K4^(3) and Fano pieces, neither touching hubs, nor a shared port on the removed line, nor the removed line's hub decides this, and chains of K4^(3) pieces create nothing.

results.title: Depth is needed: simple abelian sections force rigid selection
results.statement: In every Mal'tsev law a knot is pulled back from abelian sections of its ranges, so a knot system with declared domains is linear over the abelianized domains, and if every abelian section is simple every global failure on a substrate is rigid. Hence all laws on three values that compose like cycles (all 1020 non-simple ones checked at three places) and all non-affine laws on four values are rigid, while T2(F2) shows two layers are necessary but not sufficient.

results.title: Group laws that compose like cycles keep their top rigid
results.statement: A group's coset law composes like cycles exactly when every subgroup has a unique maximal normal subgroup (18 non-abelian such groups up to order 60), and its knots are pulled back from cyclic p-group relations. For systems with declared domains the top image after any removal from a global failure is at most one line; the law is rigid at prime-order sections, and C5:C4 and D9 keep knots below the top.

results.title: The top of the whole algebra is the wrong layer; the knot keeps emergence without depth
results.statement: A simple Mal'tsev law on five values containing Z4 composes like cycles and keeps knots in its top, so the statement fails as phrased; the rigid layer is the top of each point's own section, proved when the sections come from one chain ring. A law that composes like cycles thus keeps emergence only below the top of a two-layer abelian section, whereas the knot keeps it on two values in its only layer.

results.title: A handle creates at a frozen line exactly when its single points leave the line's claims
results.statement: Around an attachment point the own arc between two ports is barred exactly when they disagree, and a frozen line claims an own arc from one port pattern but an opposite face from two. A handle creates at a frozen line exactly when a pair of its points freezes it and neither point alone excludes either claim (one direction proved, one computed), so the Fano plane, whose single points remove one pattern per other class, never uses own arcs.

results.title: The faces a handle uses are a property of its port relation
results.statement: Across 305 handles from 24 non-planar knot spaces, every port order on a ladder, the faces a handle creates through are decided by its port relation alone: whether a pair of its points pins the face's barred state while each single point keeps the face's claims. Nine signatures occur; census 58 uses its own arc exactly when the bottom port is a third point of its two lines sharing two points.

results.title: The halo can leave the faces around the attachment point
results.statement: On a ladder arm spliced onto a grid, at a junction point the frozen region of a port class runs along the arm's far long face with two-pattern claims, and the Fano plane and census 58 create there, off the faces around the attachment point; exact creation confirms this on a 21-point piece. So the halo lies on frozen lines whose claims survive the handle's single points, refuting PHASE-HALO's law of the faces around the point.
results.issue: Qualification pending: the law holds after reduction (see the FACE-CLAIM-20261103-001 closure).

results.title: A route criterion decides which gluing lines an opened handle reaches
results.statement: A three-point crossing knot at a gluing line is generated when one of the line's points separates it or a pair of the line's points, forced by the near pair and covered by the far point's excluded block, carries a two-step elimination. With a Fano handle attached at a point of plane pieces and opened by the removal, the new knots are exactly the candidates without such a route, so creation depends on the plane piece only through its transfer.

results.title: Heights compute the transfer between a split point and any line
results.statement: In a point split of a plane knot space the solutions are corner matchings, and which pairs of port patterns and gluing-line patterns occur together is decided exactly by heights: fix the line's corner, project the difference constraints onto six regions by shortest paths, and test parities by halving. This makes the halo computable on plane pieces of hundreds of points, and it matched enumeration on all 1,221 small cases.

results.title: An opened handle is seen all along a ladder but only three steps into a grid
results.statement: An opened Fano handle attached at a point creates at the farthest gluing line of every ladder tested (prisms to 80 points) but never beyond distance 3 on grids (subdivided-octahedron duals to 256 points). Fixing the handle's point leaves every ladder line with two patterns at any distance while every grid line at distance 7 or more is exactly independent of it, so the halo follows frozen against liquid forcing.

results.title: Access is local: a plane piece keeps it whatever happens elsewhere
results.statement: Plane signed systems with as many lines as odd faces have perfect matchings as solutions and the access lemma for every pinning, and in a splice an intact side acts on the cut as the point or line it replaced. So every pinning by two points of a plane piece has access wherever the removal is, and only pinnings from inside an opened handle can fail.

results.title: An opened handle creates at a distance, and the pinned three-point premise fails
results.statement: No new knot appeared unless the gluing line lies on a handle or the removal opens a handle attached at a point, which then creates at plane gluing lines out to distance 5; when the cut carries one bit, a screening lemma reduces creation to a plane knot space. Near opened handles 1,092 of 2,496 new knots are unpinned three-point knots, and four-point new knots appear inside handles, so the pinned three-point premise fails on composite spaces.

results.title: An opened handle reaches the plane through the faces opposite its attachment point
results.statement: A port is odd on its line exactly when that line takes the single skip of the face opposite the port, so every line of that face feels it. With the Fano plane as handle, every halo line beyond distance 3 lay on a face opposite the attachment point at all 126 points tested, so the reach is set by those faces' size, not by a dimer phase; census 58 can also use the point's own face.
results.issue: Qualification pending: the face law fails at junctions and holds after reduction (see FACE-CLAIM-20261103-001).

results.title: On every ladder the halo runs the full opposite face; far grid lines are independent
results.statement: The prism is the cyclic chain of consecutive triples, whose transfer matrix has powers of period 2, so every far line's transfer depends only on its parity and the halo of an opened Fano handle runs the full opposite face on every prism. On grids, far lines have the full transfer and are independent of the handle, as height ranges grow with distance while on ladders they stay zero.

results.title: Frozen means fixed height, and untouched sides beyond a cut collapse
results.statement: A port pattern freezes exactly the points whose height difference to the ports cannot vary, and a side beyond a 3-edge cut that holds neither the handle nor the gluing line can be collapsed to the vertex it lost without changing creation. In the collapsed space the halo again lies on the faces around the attachment point, so a ring spliced onto a grid shows the full ladder halo along its far face.

results.title: Rigid strips relay an opened handle, in one direction
results.statement: In a grid, strip and grid joined through two 3-edge cuts, an opened handle in the strip or the far grid creates in the first grid near its cut, from every distance along a rigid strip and at the same lines for every length, while a liquid grid screens it within three steps. The relay enters only a side split at a point there, the direction of a handle's own splice.

results.title: The creation map splits by atom
results.statement: In a space made of plane glue and atoms at 3-edge cuts, whether a removal creates at a gluing line depends only on the atoms holding the two lines, since every other atom acts as the vertex it replaced (proved for atoms attached at a point, checked exactly for atoms attached at a line on 13 designs). So each removal's halo is its own atom's, and atoms attached at a line have no halo on plane glue.

results.title: Native selection counts and locates handles that plane glue separates
results.statement: The lines outside a largest creation-free set fall into one piece per atom, each piece an atom, when plane glue separates the atoms (416 of 420 separated spaces with two or three atoms), while touching atoms merge. On the 32 three-fold spaces up to 22 points, where atoms mostly touch, this count equals the genus in 10, and exploratory blocks of mutual creation equal it in 29.

results.title: Wires overlap halos without blurring the native count
results.statement: On small plane networks, a rigid strip or a hub lands one atom's halo on a second atom's cut lines in every placement tested (13 exact on the strip, 24 at the hub). Yet each halo stays its own atom's and the native count is unchanged: one piece per atom in all 11 separated strip placements, since a halo changes neither the quiet glue nor the lines the glue creates at.

results.title: Arc signals are wires: aligned stations repeat a relay without loss
results.statement: After a frozen hop a relay is an arc signal, two ports fixed and disagreeing, and an arc signal freezes exactly the lines with a corner on the own arc between them. So a station passes it on exactly when its out-line lies on that arc: aligned chains repeat it without loss and carry relays four cuts deep, misaligned ones stop it, and at separated cuts every creation k cuts away passed cut k as a live signal.

results.title: Relays broadcast through hubs and never run upstream
results.statement: A hub receiving an opened handle's relay copies it into every receiver its frozen region reaches, so one handle is read in several grids at once, and no relay ever creates upstream of the handle's piece. Stations with adjacent cut vertices are bypassed without loss; on three small networks exact creation confirms the broadcast, a three-cut chain and a two-cut relay.

results.title: Native creation keeps each Fano atom whole and reads each cut's direction
results.statement: A Fano atom's lines create at one another in both directions, as in the complete Fano plane (proved for atoms attached at a line by the screening lemma, computed for atoms attached at a point). Across a cut between two atoms, the receiver's cut lines and the emitter's lines are mutual while its intact lines create one way at the emitter's (676 of 676 pairs), and lines sharing two points are silent.

results.title: The tight-cut tree fixes creation between atoms joined through atoms
results.statement: On 50 spaces, the native relation between two atom lines is a function of their place in the decomposition wherever the atoms are the same, adjacent or joined through atoms only (21 places, 10,074 pairs), with fixed rules for chains, siblings and co-receivers, while through plane glue it can depend on more. The source rule fixed from these rules counts the Heawood braces, and the genus, on all 47 spaces without a non-Fano brace.

results.title: Native creation reads the genus of every fresh three-fold space up to 26 points
results.statement: On 111 fresh spaces (every three-fold class of 23 to 26 points and new trees of atoms), all 32,016 pairs at the dictionary's places and all 163 cuts between atoms behaved as predicted, and the source rule counted the Heawood braces, and the genus, on all 110 spaces without a non-Fano brace. The glue rule was refuted: across a Fano atom, glue lines can create (12 pairs, one class).

results.title: An intact Fano side never removes creation, and whether it adds any reduces to one pendant line
results.statement: Replacing a line by an intact Fano side never removes creation: the new knots off the side are those of the closed space, and generated knots through it have generated port shadows (proved through a tetrahedron form of the closure). That it never adds creation follows from the statement that one new point on one new line never does, which held on 117,344 cases but is not proved.

results.title: A hidden point may hang on one new line; two lines can create
results.statement: No hidden point whose exclusion sets are subcubes of the six port patterns changed creation (19 of 27 one-point profiles), while a point on two or three new lines through the line's points, such as the ports' majority, creates where the space without it does not. Every knot-space side tried, including every three-fold space up to 22 points split at a point, has only subcube points.

results.title: In Fano trees every atom is a block, and a line receives creation exactly where it touches the cut toward it
results.statement: In spaces built from Fano atoms alone, creation in the chain of atoms between two lines implies creation in the whole space, so every atom is a block and every line that touches its atom's cut toward a removal at most two atoms away receives creation from it. On every chain computed, that touching is also necessary: the dictionary is one rule, with non-creation still resting on the pendant-line statement.

results.title: The touching rule holds at every distance in Fano trees
results.statement: In every space built from Fano atoms alone, a line receives creation from a removal in another atom, at any distance, exactly when it touches its atom's cut facing the removal; with the block lemma, creation there is fixed by the tree. Proved by carrying finitely many profiles along chains: 47 occur, each leaves the cut's ports free, and on each the receiving atom alone decides (12,894 verdicts checked).

results.title: The source rule fails at six atoms
results.statement: BRACE-TREE's source rule keeps one block per atom on every Fano tree of at most five atoms, but fails at six: a receiver that takes two cuts from emitters feeding further receivers, and emits the line through those cuts' points, has no line blind to both loads, so its block has no source. Exact creation maps of six- and seven-atom counterexamples confirm the failure.

results.title: Native creation reads the directed tree of Fano trees
results.statement: In every Fano tree whose atoms have at most four cuts, the atoms are exactly the classes of lines that create at each other and at the same other lines, and the atoms creating at a proper subset of an atom's lines are those beyond one of its receiving cuts, which gives every cut with its direction (proved). Through plane glue the rule does not extend as stated.

results.title: A Fano atom acts as one from outside
results.statement: In all 277 spaces computed (191 saved, 86 fresh; 1,065 Fano atoms), every atom line outside a Fano atom receives the same far-side vector from each of the atom's lines, though the atom's lines differ on glue lines and in what they receive. On the saved maps the far sides nest: the Fano plane and census 58 create at the same pairs, K4^(3) only where census 6 does, and census 6 without the Fano plane only at glue lines.
results.issue: Qualification pending: the second sentence, on census 6, holds only in the order in which each gluing line's points are written; that atoms act as one holds natively (see GENUS-READ-20261107-001).

results.title: Which far side creates reads the atoms through plane glue
results.statement: A four-step rule on the creation map (twins; twins among atom lines; a split into the finest parts of three or more lines that act as one far side by far side; reattachment of single port lines) returns exactly the Fano atoms of all 191 saved spaces and, frozen, of all 86 fresh ones, including the 39 where no rule using only whether creation occurs can. On the fresh spaces GLUE-READ C's two-stage rule reads 51, the source rule 68.
results.issue: Qualification pending: the rule reads these spaces only with census 6 glued in the order in which each line's points are written; with census 6 counted over its three gluings, its split step cuts every atom of six or seven lines (see GENUS-READ-20261107-001).

results.title: Creation at an atom is decided by its cut
results.statement: For a Fano atom with its other elements present, whether a removal beyond one of its cuts creates at a line of it depends only on the patterns the removal's side allows on that cut's three ports: an emitter's lines receive iff the ports may be equal; a receiver's cut line iff the other two are not forced equal, its intact line iff the side tells the ports apart. Proved exhaustively over every port relation and deeper relation.

results.title: What plane glue does to creation is local
results.statement: On 191 spaces with exact creation maps, the touching rule holds wherever the removal's side leaves the cut free and fails only where glue constrains it; a glue line joining an atom's twin class is always a doubled-square line meeting two or more of its ports, and an atom splits only by the points of a line it emits into a planar brace. Planar lines see which port a removal entered by, while atom lines do not.

results.title: Whether creation occurs cannot read every three-fold space
results.statement: A two-stage twin rule reads the atoms of every Fano tree with at most four cuts per atom (proved), of all 111 census spaces and of 57 of 80 random spaces with plane glue. In 15 random spaces, lines of two atoms meeting one planar brace are twins of the yes/no creation relation, so no rule reading only whether creation occurs returns the atoms there, though which far side creates separates every such pair.

results.title: Creation is decided at the gluing line, in two rounds
results.statement: For every near side and the four far sides of the creation map, the closure reaches exactly the crossing knots whose near and far parts meet through the gluing line: a near knot and a far knot on the same pair of line points (round one), or two round-one knots sharing a point (round two). Proved by reducing the closure to local configurations and checking all 348,376,032 of them.

results.title: One new line never adds creation, which completes the two-bit screening lemma
results.statement: Adding one point on one new not-all-equal line through two points of a near side never adds creation, whatever its signs, and with the no-loss half creation is unchanged. So an intact Fano side standing in for a line acts as that line for creation (proved from the two-round rule, all 347,149,320 local configurations checked).

results.title: In Fano trees the dictionary up to distance two is one touching rule
results.statement: In spaces built from Fano atoms alone, a line creates at another exactly when it does in the chain of their atoms, and between atoms at most two apart exactly when the receiving line touches its atom's cut toward the removal. So native creation keeps each atom whole and reads every cut in its direction, and only a transfer along longer chains remains before the source rule is a theorem.

results.title: A Fano atom with a line removed is transparent
results.statement: In every knot space, a Fano atom with any one of its lines removed sends the free relation through each of its cuts, so what it changes there does not depend on which line went. The proof joins the project's cut theorem (closed sides act as their lost elements, up to signs), the fact that the plain Fano plane is the only signed Fano knot, and an exhaustive freeness check.

results.title: A Fano atom acts as one
results.statement: In every knot space, whether a removal in a Fano atom creates at a line of another Fano atom does not depend on which of its lines went; far side by far side this is proved except at a receiving atom's cut lines with a six-pattern port relation, and on Fano trees without exception. On 277 computed spaces every such line receives exactly its closed verdict (154,165 pairs), the exception included.

results.title: Census 6 depends on how it is glued
results.statement: The creation test glues a far side's split-point lines to the gluing line's points in their listed order; the split point's signed stabilizer realizes every permutation for K4^(3), the Fano plane and census 58 but only two for census 6, which therefore has three gluings and changed with the order in 8,046 of 11,552 sampled pairs. Whether creation occurs and the other three far sides never depend on the order.

results.title: Natively a Fano atom is homogeneous
results.statement: In every Fano tree every ordered pair of lines of a Fano atom gets one native far-side vector (no K4^(3), census 6 at one gluing of three, the Fano plane, census 58), and every atom acts as one natively, so FAR-READ's split step, given native vectors, cuts every atom of six or seven lines (none of 23 Fano trees read). The native reading of Fano trees is the yes/no twin rule.

results.title: Native far sides separate atoms through glue, rows at atom lines do not
results.statement: Through K4^(3), the Fano plane and census 58 alone every Fano atom acts as one (1,065 of 1,065), and all 372 yes/no twins across atoms in 39 spaces are told apart, 114 only through their rows at glue lines. Twins on these native rows at atom lines read 234 of 277 spaces, merging atoms where they meet one plane piece.

results.title: A growing law needs a shared coin: refinement shares it, accretion must carry it
results.statement: Growth keeps a knot sphere round without a witness only by refinement, which scales an already round seed and never places a corner. Accretion must place corners, and when each turn is decided by a label-free local rule it also closes lopsided spheres, so making the four equator corners agree needs a bit carried by the process, a hidden witness under the canonical test.

results.title: Native creation fixes the atoms of every computed space
results.statement: On 191 saved and 86 fresh spaces, pair refinement (folklore 2-WL) of the native creation map, read through the order-free far sides, never puts a pair within a Fano atom and a pair across two atoms in one class, so every symmetry of the map preserves the atoms and they are definable in three-variable counting logic in each space. On whether creation occurs alone it mixes them in 42 spaces.

results.title: No uniform native rule tried reads every space
results.statement: Yes/no two-stage twins read 219 of 277 spaces and native row twins, their maximal cliques, their refinement veto and their glue-compatible version 234 each, failing only by merging atoms that meet one plane piece (32 of 38 by complete twinship). Native-twin lines of one atom never create at a common glue line in different ways (17,494 of 17,494), while 530 of 1,572 cross-atom twin pairs do.

results.title: One hidden bit per incidence lets a law lay out its own round sphere
results.statement: A local law without hidden states cannot force a round sphere: if it allows the octahedral knot sphere, it allows long capped tubes, whose knot contradictions resolution refutes in bounded width. With one hidden bit per incidence, marking straight seams between digons, a law's spheres are exactly the octahedral knot spheres at every size, so it lays out its own round sphere and a contradiction needing width Theta(sqrt n).

results.title: Native creation reads the junctions of trisum glue
results.statement: On 18 plain trisum spaces, ten held out with frozen predictions and one with four junctions, yes/no creation reads the atoms and then the junctions: a junction's two lines are the only removals outside the atoms that block each other, so up to four junctions are counted, and pair refinement fixes atoms, junctions and leaves. Across 277 planar-glue spaces the signature appears once, at the one non-planar brace's junction.

results.title: Native creation cannot see where an atom sits within its switching class
results.statement: In one held-out space with three junctions, the native creation map has a symmetry that exchanges the line carrying an atom with an unloaded line of the same cube piece and fixes every atom line. A symmetry of the glue that keeps the switching class of the signing but moves the atom induces it, so which of the two lines carries that atom is not native.
results.issue: Qualification pending: the title holds only where a symmetry of the glue moves the atom, as in seed 5. In general native creation does see where an atom sits within its switching class: removing a line of an atom creates differently at glue lines, so placements in one class give non-isomorphic native maps, and only creation between glue lines is the same (see SWITCH-READ-20261108-001).

results.title: The Fano plane is the only uniform law that contradicts itself
results.statement: A simple cubic triple system whose symmetries are transitive on its points and on its lines has a brace for its incidence graph, so by Seymour's dictionary and McCuaig's theorem the Fano plane is its only non-2-colourable case. Since non-constant uniform signs are satisfied by the all-zero assignment, the Fano plane is the only uniform knot law that contradicts itself.

results.title: A uniform law can grow flat space but not the knot's contradiction
results.statement: A law of lines and co-lines builds its own closed surface; with one kind of point it closes into a sphere only as an antiprism or a snub polyhedron of at most 60 points. With uniform signs the count never forces the knot's lines on any uniform law, and Kasteleyn signs make the knot fail only on those small spheres or antiprism chains solvable in O(log n) queries, so a deep contradiction needs a second kind of point.

results.title: One row of creation reads the contradiction away from two-vertex cuts
results.statement: On 19 random cubic glues of 8 to 10 lines with a class without solutions, one row of creation tells the classes that tie the removed line's points from the rest exactly at the lines lying in no two-vertex cut of the incidence graph, failing at all 16 that lie in one. There, removing a cut line leaves a rigid side, K4^(3) without a line, and nothing creates in the tied row or a colliding one.

results.title: Creation between glue lines singles out the contradictory class
results.statement: On every trisum glue of 8 to 12 lines, exactly one switching class has no solution, and creation between glue lines tells it apart from every other class, by a single row on the 8- and 10-line glues. Removing a line leaves its three points tied only in that class, and degenerate gluings read the tie.

results.title: A rigid hanging side hides the contradiction from creation
results.statement: At a two-line cut whose side meeting the removed line once is K4^(3) without a line, the contradictory class's restriction and the class with one sign of the other cut line changed have the same row of creation, while only the first ties the removed line's points. The side has one rigid switching class, which the contradiction must use.

results.title: Creation between glue lines does not tell switching classes apart, and sees nothing where nothing creates
results.statement: On the 8-line trisum glue, creation between glue lines separates the switching classes up to symmetry but one pair, while on the 10-line glue it takes 429 values on 576 orbits and is identical for the 190 classes where nothing creates, whose counts run from 60 to 110. At both sizes the one class whose plain spaces are three-fold has a block of its own.

results.title: Creation between glue lines sees only the switching class
results.statement: For every cubic glue and every two signings in one switching class, removing a glue line and gluing at another gives the same native creation verdict in the two plain edge-atom spaces, because an intact atom only negates its incidence and switching only complements points. Creation between glue lines is the signed glue's own creation map.

results.title: Native creation sees a signing's switching class between glue lines and its placement through the atoms
results.statement: For five trisum glues, each with two placements of its atoms in one switching class, removing a glue line and gluing at a glue line gives the same native vectors in both placements, while removing a line of an atom creates differently at glue lines, so the whole native maps are never isomorphic. TRISUM-READ's frozen statements hold on all five alternative placements.

results.title: A law that names no relation never forces an infinite board without allowing the tree
results.statement: With names the words of F2 and an identity distinction per pair, a law over a finite alphabet whose identity literals relate only the same offset of two names, and which allows an infinite board, also allows the tree, so no such law forces the plane (proved). One named relation, the commutator, with an aperiodic tile law forces exactly the plane.

results.title: Every infinite law on the tree of names has a solution that repeats nowhere
results.statement: Every infinite shift of finite type on the free group F2, over any finite alphabet, has a solution with trivial stabilizer, so under Leibniz's rule the tree is a board exactly when a law with finite windows has infinitely many solutions, and no such law forces the plane. A level law on Z/3 with solutions has no finite board exactly when its solutions drift up or down.

results.title: Bits see a three-manifold only through mod-2 cohomology
results.statement: Native networks of a triangulation see only its dual graph, and among the 32,768 symmetric bit laws on edges only trivial and parity laws survive the 2-3 and 1-4 moves, so bits see a three-manifold only through hubs and then only through its mod-2 first cohomology. The Fibonacci rule, which sees surfaces exactly, needs a negative weight to see three-manifolds, so no count of hidden witnesses realizes it.

results.title: Native gluing builds surfaces, and the fusion rules see only them
results.statement: Hub-free gluing of three-place knots builds compact orientable surfaces, while two-place relations build only lines and loops, and exactly four knots see only the surface with counts: the parity and Fibonacci fusion rules, with one hidden bit per handle and Verlinde dimensions 2, 5, 15, 50. Hub-free gadgets never create parity, so memory must be present from the start.

results.title: The moves force a groupoid, and counting sees only finite quotients
results.statement: On ordered triangulations, a counting law whose long edge is a function of the two short edges survives the moves exactly when its working triangles form a finite groupoid with equal component values; the objects are the idempotent labels. Its count is a sum of |Hom(pi1(M), G)|/|G|, so such laws see a three-manifold only through the finite quotients of its fundamental group.

results.title: Twists add nothing in three dimensions, and the sign survives them
results.statement: On ordered triangulations with one bit per edge, twists and orientations add nothing: exactly the seven symmetric counting laws survive the ordered moves, so counts see a three-manifold only through its mod-2 first cohomology. Positive Turaev-Viro weights for the Fibonacci and twisted Fibonacci rules cannot have full support and are pure gauge on the parity class: the sign survives the twist.

results.title: Exact self-similar laws build finitely ramified spaces
results.statement: Up to six copies, the three-bit knots that reproduce themselves with uniform counts are parity, twisted not-all-equal and two three-excluded classes; not-all-equal does so at seven. Their towers keep the corner law at every scale with growth exponents log2 3, 2 and log3 7, but are finitely ramified, and softening is repelled at least threefold per level.

results.title: Only parity survives native patterns of patterns
results.statement: Among Boolean knots glued natively, only parity is rebuilt by gadgets of its own copies: other three-place knots' gadgets exclude fewer tuples, so towers of patterns of patterns go free within three levels, and at four places (up to three copies) only parity and one chained implication between pair parities survive. No three-place knot orients a vertex and no orienting four-place knot survives, so native laws fix topology but neither orientation nor scale.

results.title: Not-all-equal survives patterns of patterns through the Fano plane
results.statement: With hubs, not-all-equal is rebuilt by its copies on the seven lines of the Fano plane with one point split into the legs, and no smaller hub gadget rebuilds it, so its smallest pattern of patterns is a finite projective plane; every allowed tuple has exactly five completions, an exact counted fixed point. Within six copies, hub gadgets rebuild exactly seven of the sixteen three-bit knot classes, all through copies in parallel.

results.title: The two/three boundary is a boundary of positivity
results.statement: With nonnegative values no such sum has a three-bit knot as its support, however many hidden bits it uses; with signed values every one of the 16 classes of three-bit knots is exactly such a sum with one hidden bit, and a clause of any width is one hidden bit (inclusion-exclusion). So the program's rule that two-variable constraints never make a knot holds exactly as long as witnesses cannot cancel.

results.title: Signed laws survive native coarse-graining
results.statement: Where nonnegative counting reproduces only parity, signed laws of 14 of the 16 knot classes are rebuilt and 12 are reproduced exactly, 10 of them by the native triangle that generates the Sierpinski gasket, so signed not-all-equal persists at every scale. The two Fibonacci fusion knots are never rebuilt, and on closed spheres the shared-boundary substitution still keeps only parity.

results.title: On genuine two-dimensional space only parity reproduces itself with a knot
results.statement: On the triangular lattice with shared subdivision, only 22 of 122 knot rules reproduce themselves exactly at scale 2 and 6 at scale 3, all with affine solution sets and zero entropy density: parity (Newman-Moore, Baxter-Wu), rules equal to parity on tori, and twisted not-all-equal collapsed to equality lines. Exactness on genuine two-dimensional space keeps a knot only through parity; not-all-equal never reproduces itself.

results.title: Interference adds one phase and no relation in three dimensions
results.statement: Every signed one-bit edge law with weights in {-1, 0, 1} invariant under the ordered 2-3 and 1-4 moves has a counting support, and up to sign changes it is a counting law, the twisted Dijkgraaf-Witten law (-1)^(x01 x12 x23) on a cocycle support, or a mix of these. No twisted law is symmetric, so signs need the vertex order, as order alone added nothing to counting.

results.title: Signed bits see one bit of the linking form
results.statement: The twisted laws compute the Gauss sum of the cubic form a -> a^3 on H^1(M; Z/2), which is linear, so they see exactly whether the linking form gives 1/2 on an element of order 2. That bit is not a function of homology: it separates RP^3 # RP^3 from S^3/Q_8 and sampled triangulations that every counting law identifies.

results.title: A knot builds exactly self-similar space of every dimension below two
results.statement: Signed not-all-equal, (-1)^a times the Legendre symbol of a+b+c mod 3, reproduces itself exactly on every level-k Sierpinski gasket, with a factor congruent to ±1 mod 3, because its two Eisenstein phase sectors stay locked along the gasket's edges. It therefore builds exact self-similar spaces of dimension log(k(k+1)/2)/log k for every k, approaching two, while shared subdivision of the plane admits no such knot.

results.title: Gaskets select only the standing wave and parity
results.statement: Of 1,168 signed three-bit laws, 68 are exact on some gasket up to level 12, and every one that persists is a rotation, relabeling or field twist of the Eisenstein standing wave, or linear parity at powers of two. The other 42 are single-level coincidences at levels 3 and 5.

results.title: Interference builds no new exact law on genuine two-dimensional space
results.statement: Under shared subdivision of the triangular lattice, weights ±1 make no shape outside the 22 affine exact ones exact, even on allowed states, and real weights add none wherever decidable: positive weights keep the counted supports, a sign-parity obstruction excludes 54 of the 100 non-affine shapes for every weighting, and the affine shapes' exact real weightings are gauge copies of the ±1 laws. Exact self-reproduction on genuine two-dimensional space stays affine; 46 dense shapes remain open.

results.title: A knot builds exactly self-similar space in every dimension
results.statement: The standing wave (-1)^(x_0) sin(theta E)/sin(theta) reproduces itself exactly on every level-k Sierpinski d-simplex, with a factor that is a monic integer polynomial in 2 cos(theta), equal to 2^N at theta = 0 and never zero at odd prime-power angles. Its Legendre member is an exact knot in every dimension d >= 2, and in odd d the whole family is, so knots build exact self-similar spaces whose dimension rises to d in every dimension.

results.title: Only standing waves persist on Sierpinski tetrahedra
results.statement: The cosine wave (-1)^(x_0) cos(theta E) reproduces itself exactly when the number of simplices is odd and otherwise turns into the sine wave, which explains the period-4 family of the plane. In exact censuses on Sierpinski tetrahedra and four-simplices the only knots exact at every computed level are standing waves, and the wave's rational exceptional angles are only pi/2 and, at even levels, pi/4.

results.title: Four gasket levels force the standing wave
results.statement: A three-bit law symmetric in its two non-base corners reproduces itself on the Sierpinski gaskets of levels 2 to 5 exactly when it is a standing wave, a product, an equal-corner law or one of two frozen laws, and then it does so at every level. Fewer levels admit impostors: a whole curve at levels 2 and 3, and 16 complex laws at levels 2 to 4.

results.title: Implication laws build every gasket, but no knot except the wave does
results.statement: Besides rotations of the symmetric classes, general three-bit laws reproducing themselves on gasket levels 2 to 5 include the implication laws, two-sector laws whose support is a one-way implication; they compose like a chain and build every gasket. In the classified strata the only knots that do so are signed not-all-equal and its rotations.

results.title: A beginning is a knot: a growth order never knots with the world
results.statement: Written into a law, a growth history never knots with the world's states: on a fixed world the two form a product, and when worlds vary, with absent things forgotten, every knot containing an order variable contains an existence variable, which enters as a presence literal. The history's local part, which neighbour came first, is pairwise (2-CNF) and holds no knot, while time without a loop is a law whose knots are exactly the world's cycles, so on a ring the beginning is one not-all-equal knot over every seam, which the pairwise part contradicts. By Euler's count, sprouting grows only trees and disc moves only discs and spheres, and in one dimension the beginning does what no bounded static witness can: no radius-r law with bounded hidden labels tells a long thread from a ring.

results.title: Without ends, bond distance is a ruler that reads the lattice's dimension
results.statement: If a law's finitely supported moves are dense (no ends), every knot is chained at the moves' range, so bond distance grows linearly with separation and its balls recover the lattice's dimension from allowed states alone, with taxicab distance on the gauge plane and exactly t-s+1 along the atom thread. Per-variable nativity is not enough: Ledrappier's law plus a free field is native in every variable yet has knots joining points 2^k apart.

results.title: Ledrappier's frozen plane measures distance in signed bits
results.statement: In Ledrappier's law the three-place knots are exactly the Frobenius triangles, so every point has bond-distance-2 neighbours at every power-of-two separation and every bond ball is infinite. Along each lattice line the bond distance between points n apart is at most 1 + w(n), the weight of n's non-adjacent form, and equals 2 exactly at powers of two.

results.title: Open ends make a substitution tower stretch
results.statement: A hub-free parity substitution keeps the replaced knot exactly when its gadget adds no open end, and then every step is conservative, so the original distinctions stay at bond distance 2 forever; this is why the 2026-10-20 refinement cannot grow space. On tree-shaped knot graphs bond distance equals the path's knot count plus one, so the star tower stretches as 3^k + 1.

results.title: Periodic logic makes polygons with rational pi
results.statement: For a parity law on a doubly periodic plane graph, bond distance is twice the graph distance of the plane dual up to a constant, so its circle is half the dual's velocity polygon, with rational vertices and a rational pi (half its perimeter measured with its own distance). By Niven's theorem its only regular circles are the hexagon (pi = 3) and the parallelogram (pi = 4), and no periodic law has a round circle.

results.title: Laws on lines reach the circle only as a limit
results.statement: With a four-place parity knot at each crossing of a line arrangement, bond distance is twice the number of lines separating two segments, plus a bounded amount. With n equally spaced, equally dense directions the circle is a regular 2n-gon whose pi is Archimedes' inscribed or circumscribed value, 2n sin(pi/2n) or 2n tan(pi/2n): irrational from n = 4 on, periodic only for n = 2, 3, and 5/phi for the Penrose pentagrid.

results.title: Coins bend logical circles; only isotropy makes them round
results.statement: When coins split each four-place knot of the square parity law into two three-place knots, distance in the plane dual is exactly the coordinate sum minus the longest strictly increasing chain of matching squares and bond distance is twice it at large scale, so the circle is a square with elliptic corners, quarter circles for fair coins (pi = 3.44120), whose flat lattice sides persist. A parity law on a Poisson-Voronoi tessellation, with no preferred direction, is exactly round.

results.title: A local rule grows the logical number line
results.statement: Starting from one parity knot, growing only at knots that hold two or more open ends grows exactly the two-way thread, a path of knots each keeping one open loop, whatever choices are made. Its bond distance counts the knots between two points plus one, so a rule that reads nothing but open ends grows a ruler of dimension one in both directions.

results.title: Closing open ends seals or collapses space
results.statement: In hub-free parity laws bond distance is the least two-sided boundary, counting seams and open ends held inside, so every such boundary is a knot. A region without open ends behind one seam pins it and no knot crosses, and a long region with a short boundary keeps bond distance bounded; closing rules therefore freeze space into cells or collapse it.

results.title: The logical Cartesian plane is a taxicab plane
results.statement: In the product law of two parity laws, a knot of each axis joined at a corner is a knot, so bond distance is at most the sum of the axis distances minus one. The product of two two-way threads has no ends, so its bond distance is within constants of taxicab distance and its bond balls grow quadratically: a plane of dimension two built from two lines.

results.title: The pinwheel's radius-2 law reads its own labels
results.statement: On every pinwheel tiling, the radius-2 neighbourhoods of darts in the unlabelled planar map take exactly 1,168 forms, each fixing its edge's oriented label (side types, intervals, direction), so the labels that drive the eleven-label regrowth rule are read from the bare map within radius 2. The proof closes the 193 collared tiles under the cut and cuts each of the 108 complete ones four times; at radius 1 there are 198 forms, 9 of them ambiguous.

results.title: A finite rule on knots grows the pinwheel law
results.statement: Label each distinction of the pinwheel's parity law by its two knots' side types, its place along them and whether they run the same way: only eleven labels occur, and a fixed table (every knot into five, every distinction into the pieces its label names, five new distinctions per knot) regrows the law exactly at every level. No coordinate or angle enters the rule, and the only T-junctions are at midpoints of long legs.
results.issue: Qualification pending: the rule is known in substance. Kenyon and Stephenson (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 147, 2019) give the pinwheel a coordinate-free subdivision rule with four-cornered tiles, the fourth corner at the long leg's midpoint. New here are the rule's form on a parity law's knots and distinctions, its eleven-label alphabet and its exact check (see the PINWHEEL-NATIVE-20261107-001 decision note).

results.title: A law with no coins has a round circle
results.statement: On Conway and Radin's pinwheel tiling, the parity laws with knots at tile corners or on tiles have bond distances, counts of distinctions with no lengths, that grow at the same rate in every direction: exactly round circles with no chance involved. The proof is an isotropy principle: a rotation-invariant tiling space uniquely ergodic under translations makes every covariant bond distance round.

results.title: Roundness needs an irrational turn and mirror pairs
results.statement: Cutting a right triangle into copies of itself gives a round logical circle only when its angle is an irrational part of a turn and siblings come in both handednesses: legs 1:1 give the periodic tetrakis triangulation with polygonal circles (pi = 10/3 and 4), and the 1:2 triangle cut frame-consistently keeps one frame. Even the pinwheel is round only as a trend, meeting O(log R) orientations within radius R.

results.title: Chains of knots part from bond distance only at gates
results.statement: On parity laws a chain of knots always holds a knot through its ends, so chain measures collapse or equal bond distance. Off parity laws they part exactly at gates, where one value of a shared distinction satisfies both knots, so the NAND thread is a line for chain distance and none for bond distance.

results.title: A periodic plane obeys every undecorated local law of the pinwheel
results.statement: Four 1:2 right triangles around a common right angle make a rhombus, and the lattice tiling by these rhombi, cut once by Conway's cut, is a periodic tiling whose every collar occurs in pinwheel tilings; its further cuts make every patch of any fixed radius a pinwheel patch, so no undecorated local law of the pinwheel forces aperiodicity.

results.title: The pinwheel's collar law forces one level of its hierarchy
results.statement: In every tiling whose collars all occur in pinwheel tilings, each collar names its tile's parent and touching siblings agree, so the tiling is the cut of a tiling by larger triangles whose collars lie in a finite level-one law of 1,264 collars per handedness; that law admits the rhombus lattice, so composition is forced one level and no further.

results.title: One hidden bit per tile never forces the pinwheel
results.statement: Every one of the 1,024 decorated substitutions of the pinwheel on two labels admits a periodic plane obeying its law at every radius. The last falls to crystals built from its surviving parent collars, the smallest with 8 tiles per period, half of them turned by twice the pinwheel angle from the other half.

results.title: One hidden bit per tile rarely forces the pinwheel
results.statement: Labels read from a bounded window of the pinwheel tiling never force aperiodicity, and of the 1,024 decorated substitutions on two labels 1,008 still admit a periodic plane at every radius, a cut rhombus or brick crystal with a periodic labelling; in the other 16 the bit forces every parent's label, but pairwise consistency leaves labelled parent collars outside the law, so whether one of them forces the pinwheel is open.

results.title: Fair distinctions make not-all-equal worlds a percolation problem at exactly 1/2
results.statement: Recoloured, fair visible distinctions orient the hidden implications of a not-all-equal world by coin flips, reach through them is bond percolation at exactly 1/2, and a world without a directed crossing of its cut torus in one direction is consistent. So global emergence vanishes below a lattice's bond threshold, stays bounded on the square lattice, where self-duality puts the threshold at 1/2, and diverges when two-way contacts percolate.

results.title: Exactly two fair contacts are critical on the square lattice, and one is bipartite percolation
results.statement: Among 204 placements of three-variable knots as fair contacts on square-lattice tori, six classes have a vacuum and hold nothing, parity and swap-or-order frustrate locally, and only not-all-equal and 'x or (h ≠ h′)' hold purely global emergence. The latter is consistent exactly when its disequality edges, bond percolation at 1/2, are bipartite, so its emergence is bounded on both sides and is a torus winding quantity that Pinson's conformal formula predicts.

results.title: Not-all-equal emergence is strongly-connected percolation on twisted tori, with an exact duality
results.statement: A fair not-all-equal world is inconsistent exactly when the swap-reversed random orientation of its bipartite double cover has a swap-invariant strongly connected component, that is when its cyclic edges form a cross cluster or an odd winding. On twisted tori primal and dual cyclic edges are exactly complementary, so P(all contractible) = P(cross) and the emergence lies between -log2(1 - P0) and -log2 P0.

results.title: Directed winding on toroidal orientations obeys an exact polar duality
results.statement: On any square-lattice torus, the primitive classes of an orientation's directed closed walks are exactly those in a closed convex cone, and the rotated dual orientation realizes exactly those in its polar; the uniform orientation's cone has a polar-invariant law. So the conjecture that strongly-connected percolation wraps in one direction with probability 3/4 is equivalent to: with probability 1/4, no directed closed walk winds horizontally.

results.title: A doubled edge hides the sign of a parallel path from acyclic counts
results.statement: Flipping the sign of a path through degree-2 vertices whose ends are also joined by links of both signs keeps a signed graph's chromatic polynomial, and so its number of acyclic orientations, though not its Tutte polynomial. One such flip explains each of the 48 skeletons that isomorphic pieces left unexplained on L(3,1,3,1), so every exact twist relation found on the genus-2 surfaces now holds skeleton by skeleton.

results.title: Two-literal contradictions are all or nothing in direction
results.statement: In every two-literal tiling world on a triangular torus, shared coins included, a configuration contradicts along no class, one class, or every class its twist makes odd, so three cylinders certify a lone line there. Three-place worlds can contradict along some odd classes and not others, so their lone lines need not be lines, which inflated the dual-pair ratios previously reported, although lines pure among eight classes still differ.

results.title: A lone loop shields exactly the twist dual to it
results.statement: On every closed orientable surface, the probability that the twisted strong components wind along a class c and nothing else is the same for a twist and for that twist plus the dual of c, under fair orientations, by a wall involution along the loop. Seams next to a lone loop carry only that dual twist (Lefschetz duality), and in three dimensions no wall exists around a loop.

results.title: A lone odd loop shields the transverse twist
results.statement: On every square-lattice torus, at every shear and for every primitive class c, the two twists odd on c give exactly the same probability that the twisted strong components wind along c and nothing else, for fair orientations. An explicit involution proves it: sliding the second twist's seam onto the upper boundary of the odd loop, with bit flips on edges entered from the free side, changes no directed cycle.

results.title: Shielding is a law of coins that reach two places
results.statement: In twisted fair worlds on tori, a lone contradiction line has the same count in the two twists odd on its class whenever each coin decides a contact on two places, a theorem on every torus. Exact enumeration of the smallest tori finds every pair not related by symmetry unequal once one coin decides three places, through a three-place relation or two clauses sharing it: the line falls at a coin's reach, not clause width.

results.title: Three-place contradictions wind where the twist is odd
results.statement: For fair contacts with three hidden places, a twist is a cohomology class exactly when flipping all three places swaps the contact's two relations. When the doubly allowed patterns tile the plane, no planar patch and no fitting twist contradicts, and every minimal contradiction on a torus winds, along classes on which the twist differs from every fitting twist.

results.title: A twist reaches a count only through two small pieces
results.statement: On every closed surface, the number of fair orientations whose cyclic edges form a given skeleton is, in each twist, the number of orientations of the skeleton with every edge cyclic times the number of acyclic orientations of the graph with each cluster shrunk to a point. Walls are odd clusters, and for any rank they leave the counts unchanged under the duals of the radical of the cluster's lattice.

results.title: The twist sectors split into whole and half-integer harmonics of the shear
results.statement: On square-lattice tori, shearing by the width relabels the four twist sectors and the mirror maps each sector to itself, for every orientation, so the effect of the second twist splits into a part with whole harmonics of the shear and a part with only half-integer harmonics that vanishes at half shear. Additivity of P(all strong components contractible) across the sectors is therefore a relation of one basis, dephased by any shear, and it is not exact at finite size.

results.title: Walls, not algebra, decide which three-place contacts are rigid in direction
results.statement: At three places, rigidity in direction is decided by the geometry of walls, not by algebra: all three-place tiling contacts have trivial polymorphisms, and renaming the places of one relation can change its kind. Contacts with free stripes or straight pinned walls are rigid on every torus, with an exact count; the twelve whose walls can turn are selective, and when their walls have no choices a direction contradicts exactly where every wall collides with its own copy.

results.title: Directed walls make reading a direction polynomial
results.statement: For the six directed three-place tiling contacts, whether a direction contradicts is decided in polynomial time: their walls are monotone paths whose good walls form a lattice, Aubry's ordered maximum and a split shorten any good wall to one that is simple on the cover undoing the twist, and max-closed constraints decide each period. Among the bending contacts only the four honeycomb ones with a free place now lack a polynomial rule.

results.title: Periodic walls that avoid their own copies decide every direction
results.statement: For every three-place tiling contact with a constant frame, a direction has an assignment exactly when some periodic wall crosses its cylinder without meeting its own copies; the rule needs no determinism, because a cylinder with an assignment has a periodic one. Planted staircases make eight of the twelve bending contacts selective on every torus with sides at least 3; for the other four, good walls must sometimes repeat a state, and selectivity on every torus is open.

results.title: S4 colourings of knots are #P-hard; metabelian targets stay polynomial with bounded homology
results.statement: Counting homomorphisms from knot groups (first homology Z) to S4 that send meridians to transpositions is #P-hard: on tripled alternating diagrams of plane graphs the S3 colourings are free potentials, and the S4 lifts follow the left-right cycles of each monochromatic subgraph, giving a twelve-state model equal to the 12-state Potts model at v = 1/2 for links. Every group with an abelian normal subgroup and nilpotent quotient stays polynomial with bounded mod-p homology.

results.title: The two connected quandles of order 6 colour every knot equally
results.statement: Every S4 transposition colouring of a knot has trivial longitude, and over each S3 colouring the twisted lifting cohomology meets the boundary torus in a line over the meridian (half-lives-half-dies), so transposition and 4-cycle lifts are equinumerous. Hence the connected quandles C[6,1] and C[6,2] colour every classical knot equally, proving the 2013 conjecture of Clark, Elhamdadi, Hou, Saito and Yeatman for this pair; a virtual knot shows the 3-manifold input is needed.

results.title: S4 counting is #P-hard on closed manifolds with first homology Z/2
results.statement: For every knot, the S4 counts of 2- and 4-surgery satisfy C2 + C4 = 8 + 3T, and 3 C2(K) + C2(K # trefoil) = 16 + 12T, where T counts transposition colourings. With the independently replayed knot hardness, counting homomorphisms to S4 is #P-hard on closed 3-manifolds with first homology Z/2, where metabelian targets stay polynomial.

results.title: Root fillings separate the order-16 collision; the full dichotomy was already known
results.statement: Dehn-filling parallel copies of the edge curves by square roots kills the reflection channels of the order-16 dihedral group, so interpolation recovers 4^m 8 P(G,4)/2^|V|, and an index-p theorem gives explicit chromatic coefficients for every group with an abelian normal subgroup of prime index acting nontrivially on its p-th powers. Hardness for every non-abelian group already follows from Galindo's 2026 Turaev-Viro dichotomy, which also predates HARD-3D-20261025-001's novelty claims.

results.title: Counting maps from 3-manifold groups into S3 is #P-hard, and doubles count pairs of colourings
results.statement: Counting homomorphisms from 3-manifold groups into S3 is #P-hard: handlebodies with tori attached along a planar graph turn it into a spin model that recovers 3-colourings, and their closed doubles count pairs of colourings, 2 P(G,9)/3^|V|. The same holds on closed manifolds for most dihedral groups, Q8 and A4, so for class-2 targets bounded H2 is needed.

results.title: SL(2,3) is polynomial with bounded homology; the line is not abelian-by-nilpotent
results.statement: SL(2,3) is polynomial on closed 3-manifolds with bounded first homology: its maps are A4 maps forming affine twisted-cocycle spaces over boundedly many maps to Z3, and the lift through the centre is obstructed by a quadratic function into the bounded group H^2(M; F2), whose zeros Gauss sums count. Since SL(2,3) is not abelian-by-nilpotent while S4 and its double covers are #P-hard, the bounded-homology line separates Fitting heights 2 and 3 as far as tested.

results.title: A dichotomy for Heisenberg-by-cyclic groups with bounded homology, and a counterexample to Rowell's conjecture
results.statement: For Heisenberg groups over odd prime fields with a coprime cyclic action, counting homomorphisms from 3-manifold groups with bounded first homology is #P-hard exactly when the action's three characters are nontrivial (else polynomial), already on knot surgeries and knot groups, because Borromean moves steer a three-way eigen-triple form into a Potts gadget. Hence Rowell's 2009 conjecture of polynomial exact counting on link groups for solvable targets fails, also for S4, unless #P functions are polynomial-time computable.

results.title: SL(2,3) is polynomial with bounded homology; the line is the twisting, not the Fitting height
results.statement: SL(2,3) is polynomial on closed 3-manifolds with bounded first homology: its maps are A4 maps forming affine twisted-cocycle spaces, and the central lift is obstructed by a quadratic function into the bounded group H^2(M; F2), counted by Gauss sums. The bounded-homology line is not the Fitting height: UT3(F4) x| C3, also of Fitting height 2, is #P-hard because its twisted obstruction is a free three-way form.

results.title: A re-proof of Livingston's equinumerosity by twisted lifting cohomology
results.statement: Every S4 transposition colouring of a knot has trivial longitude, and over each S3 colouring the transposition and 4-cycle lifts are equinumerous, re-proving Livingston's 1995 Theorems 8 and 9 by twisted lifting cohomology. Hence the connected quandles C[6,1] and C[6,2] colour every knot equally; the 2013 conjecture of Clark, Elhamdadi, Hou, Saito and Yeatman for this pair was already implied by Livingston.

results.title: Fin manifolds and their doubles count colourings: explicit S3 and dihedral constructions
results.statement: Handlebodies with tori attached along a planar graph turn counting maps into S3 into a spin model that recovers 3-colourings, and their closed doubles count pairs of colourings, 2 P(G,9)/3^|V|, with analogous chromatic formulas for most dihedral groups, Q8 and A4. The resulting #P-hardness is a case of Galindo's 2026 Turaev-Viro dichotomy; the explicit chromatic constructions are the contribution.

results.title: A Fitting-height-2 group is #P-hard with bounded homology and on knot groups
results.statement: Counting homomorphisms from 3-manifold groups with H1 = Z/3, and from knot groups, into UT3(F4) x| C3, a solvable group of Fitting height 2, is #P-hard: the twisted obstruction is one cubic form whose alternating part Borromean moves steer freely, and an edge gadget turns its kernel count into a Potts partition function. So the bounded-homology line is not the Fitting height, and Rowell's 2009 conjecture fails for this group unless #P functions are polynomial-time computable.

results.title: A Fitting-height-2 group is #P-hard with bounded homology: the twisted triple product
results.statement: Counting homomorphisms from 3-manifold groups with H1 = Z/3 into UT3(F4) x| C3, a solvable group of Fitting height 2, is #P-hard: the twisted obstruction is one cubic form whose alternating part Borromean moves steer freely, and an edge gadget turns its kernel count into a Potts partition function. So with bounded homology the easy/hard line is not the Fitting height but pairwise versus three-way twisted obstructions.

results.title: Past class 2, hardness needs no three-way pair: a four-way Massey interaction is #P-hard where no pair can be
results.statement: For coprime p-group-by-cyclic targets on closed 3-manifolds with bounded first homology, hardness past class 2 does not need a three-way pair: a cross-layer hard pair already gives #P-hardness, and at r = 2, where no hard pair exists and class 2 is always polynomial, counting maps from 2-surgeries on knots into U4(F_p) x| <diag(1,-1,1,-1)> (p >= 5) is #P-hard, carried by a twisted triple Massey product read against a fourth class.

results.title: A dichotomy for counting maps to class-(K) groups with bounded homology, on closed manifolds and knot groups
results.statement: For coprime class-2-by-cyclic groups of class (K) over odd prime fields with r | p - 1, counting homomorphisms from closed 3-manifold groups with bounded first homology, and from knot groups, is #P-hard exactly when a commutator joins two nontrivial characters with nontrivial product (else polynomial), via sector partition functions isolated over disjoint unions and Bulatov-Grohe. Hence Rowell's 2009 conjecture fails for every such group unless every #P function is polynomial-time computable.

results.title: Pairs collapse the cyclic action to an involution and triples decide: counting maps to nilpotent-by-cyclic groups at every sector order
results.statement: For p-groups of exponent p with a coprime cyclic action, counting maps from closed 3-manifolds with H1(M; F_p) = 0 is polynomial at a sector order whenever nontrivial characters bracket only with their inverses, collapsing the action to an involution, and that involution's Lie triple system is abelian; for graded class at most 4 it is #P-hard when pairs hold and a triple survives, at every sector order. Pair failures in classes 3-4 remain open.

results.title: Counting maps to nilpotent-by-cyclic groups sees only the ideal of nonzero characters, and inert layers transfer hardness
results.statement: On closed 3-manifolds without F_p-homology, every map over a sector of order d lands in the subgroup generated by the nonzero-character part, so trivial-character generators drop out and the earlier cross-layer example is explained. Hardness passes from any quotient with a pinned surgery construction whose knots avoid the kernel's characters, which decides 153 of 329 residual census algebras.

results.title: Pair failures that interact with higher layers are #P-hard when the edge is clean: a Brunnian rank lemma
results.statement: Gadget knots whose blocks return exactly to the meridian value make the count an edge-local integer partition function whose edge count is maximal on the diagonal, where the Borromean insertion is trivial, and strictly smaller across a pair-failing difference. So higher layers cannot cancel hardness, and with a character-0 refinement this decides 55 interacting census algebras.

results.title: Vertex conservation laws need not block hardness: conserved flows with a non-negative Fourier dual
results.statement: When a gadget vertex reads the bracket of an edge's own leaves, its equations form a flow conserved at every vertex, and Fourier duality turns the count into a spin system on vertex states and potentials. If the flow vanishes off the diagonal and is bilinear on it, the weights are non-negative and the Brunnian rank witness gives #P-hardness, deciding 8 more census algebras.

results.title: At r = 2 the Lie triple system decides: counting maps to nilpotent-by-involution groups is polynomial iff it is abelian
results.statement: For p-groups of exponent p with an involution, counting maps from closed 3-manifold groups with H1(M; F_p) = 0 is polynomial whenever the Lie triple system of the minus part is abelian, in every class, since every homomorphism then lies in a class-2 subgroup; and for graded algebras of class at most 4 it is #P-hard otherwise, already on 2-surgeries of knots. So at r = 2 brackets of two minus elements never matter and brackets of three decide.

results.title: Linear flows: vertex-root pair failures are #P-hard when the dual slot has no degree-1 data
results.statement: When a class-3 edge fails only the vertex-root condition and its dual slot carries no degree-1 data, the conserved vertex flow and the dual slot's constraints are linear in that slot's data, so every Fourier-dual weight counts solutions of linear equations and is non-negative. With the Brunnian rank witness this gives #P-hardness, deciding 8 more census algebras and, with conserved flows, the whole vertex-root family.

results.title: Class-4 pair failures are #P-hard if gadget counts are local up to a Massey-type relabeling
results.statement: If zero-jump gadget counts are local up to a relabeling of degree-3 data, the indeterminacy of a Massey-type obstruction, then linear flows on single edges keep the Fourier dual non-negative even with independent potentials at the two ends of an edge, so counting is #P-hard. Six class-4 census algebras satisfy the single-edge conditions, so they are #P-hard if that locality holds.

results.title: The smallest knot space that counts writes the count in binary
results.statement: The eight-point torus that computes the parity of three held points also reads their majority at another point, so it holds their count as two binary digits, a full adder, at the least size at which any knot space counts (exact). Such spaces hold a count mod m only for even m and an odd number of held points, so counting in threes needs a value fixed from outside (proved).

results.title: Bases within bases keep the law and spread no influence
results.statement: Stitched at one place, harmonies standing in for distinctions keep the outer law exactly at every level, never end, and only multiply the seed's forced values, and only the alternation 0101 is one distinction exactly (proved). A drawn three-copy nesting forces nothing to level 7 (exact).

results.title: The knot law's repeats have no odd period up to 29
results.statement: No base of not-all-equal knots along one shift, at any span and with any number of knot kinds, whose allowed states all repeat has a state of odd period up to 29 (computer-assisted). The mirror alone does not forbid odd periods; what does is a value that can flip unseen, and a word of odd period without one would itself make such a base.

results.title: Knot-law repeats of odd length at 73 and 193
results.statement: Not-all-equal knot kinds forbidding three equal values at equal spacing with steps 1, 2, 27 and 54 modulo 73, or with six steps modulo 193, allow only states repeating with period 73, or 193 (proved): two more odd harmonies after 61. In two structured step families they are the only odd periods to 199, and each has steps closed under a fourth root of 1.

results.title: A knot-law repeat of odd length: period 61
results.statement: Twelve not-all-equal knot kinds, forbidding three equal values at equal spacing with step 1, 2, 11 or 22 modulo 61, allow only states that repeat with period 61 (proved): an odd harmony. No such base has an odd period up to 29 or at 31 or 37, so the knot law's repeats are not all even.

results.title: Braun's formal Res(⊕) bit-PHP bound states what the paper claims
results.statement: The Lean statement behind Braun's claimed exponential lower bound for the bit pigeonhole principle in DAG-like Res(⊕) covers every standard rule set (any sound inference from two earlier lines, reuse unrestricted, every line counted) and exactly the usual clauses with 2^l+1 pigeons. It is not vacuous: the clause set is unsatisfiable for every l, and the system refutes l = 1.

results.title: Braun's Res(⊕) bound extends to more pigeons and to bit-colouring
results.statement: For l >= 32, every DAG-like Res(⊕) refutation of bit PHP with 2^l holes and m pigeons, for 2^l < m with 8192 m l^2 (2l+5) <= 4^l, has more than exp(4^l/(8192 m l^2)) lines, checked in Lean against Braun's replayed development. A proper colouring with m classes turns every bit-colouring refutation into one of bit PHP with m pigeons of the same size, so the bound covers every graph whose chromatic number lies in that range.
results.issue: Qualification pending: for linearly many pigeons a stronger bound, exp(Ω(n)), was already in Pang's arXiv 2610.00837v1 (30 September 2026); the novelty narrows to superlinearly many pigeons, where ECCC TR26-316 (10 November 2026, Theorem 3.2) later states the same form (see AUDIT-LEFT-20261110-001).

results.title: Re-signing moves the knot sphere's forced dissonance into the law and carries it anywhere
results.statement: On every simplicial knot sphere with Kasteleyn signs, every law with exactly two even faces is satisfiable wherever they sit, so one sign change at the violated line always moves the forced dissonance out of the states and into the law. With the state held fixed, sign changes made only at the violated line or at an even face carry the dissonance from any line to any line, and a closed walk of them equals a block change of state.

results.title: Every line of a knot sphere carries the forced dissonance equally often
results.statement: On every simplicial two-coloured sphere triangulation with Kasteleyn signs, each line is the only violated line of exactly 2N(T) states with no over-agreeing face, where N(T)^2 = det(BB^T)/(n0n1 + n1n2 + n2n0) for the line-vertex matrix B and the class sizes n_i of the vertex 3-colouring. Two even faces of different colours never allow fewer consistent states than two adjacent ones.

results.title: Learning removes a class-forced dissonance only by winding around a handle
results.statement: On a torus whose Kasteleyn law is in a class no state satisfies, the least dissonance is one violated line and one over-agreeing face, and learning at the dissonance with the state fixed removes it, leaving no even face. Every process that removes it changes the law by a cycle of nonzero homology class, so learning carries the law's class, which no change of state can, and only around a handle.

results.title: Each acting Fano atom holds a unit of the leftover dissonance, and units beyond them are free
results.statement: On every one of 1,280 sign classes of 11 spaces with three or four Fano atoms, decided by SAT over every state: no state satisfies every line when every atom acts as its line, and otherwise every such state holds a unit in each acting atom, with any further units free. Which atoms act is set by each atom's own handle.

results.title: On every octahedral knot sphere, each separated Fano atom acts as its line in exactly one class of its handle and then holds a unit
results.statement: For every octahedral knot sphere with separated Fano atoms, each atom acts as its replaced line in exactly one of its handle's four classes; if all act no state satisfies every line, and otherwise every acting atom holds a unit of the floor dissonance. Proved computer-assisted: two lemmas by hand, a finite local check and a classification of line neighbourhoods.

results.title: Names read a stored class only upward, against two fixed landmarks
results.statement: Read by parity names, a closed leaf's class gives only three readings: its acting class, its acting class or its most constrained satisfiable class, or every class; with two leaves only one of nine joint minterms of the non-acting classes appears. So readings stay monotone and the basis is not completed (computed exhaustively on new networks).

results.title: Every line of a knot sphere is critical, so the layered memory computes only conjunctions
results.statement: Every line of every Kasteleyn knot sphere has a state violating it alone, since any set of lines touches at least two more faces than it has lines; with growth keeping this, a composite over any host built from knot spheres and class-forced lattice tori computes exactly the AND of its atoms' bits (proved by hand). Disturbances whose flips and repairs touch disjoint lines and faces combine in every order.

results.title: A learned knot memory reads which of its atoms hold, and learns gates through composites by trial
results.statement: With its stall fixed, a learner seeing only its dissonance under the world's clamps learned 10 of 16 composite gates by trial, not 1 (computed). Dissonance a state-only walk cannot clear marked acting atoms without error, but as credit it did not raise the total (computed).

results.title: Cuts and names read AND and OR of stored bits, but no negation was found
results.statement: An unsatisfiable component makes the whole network unsatisfiable and a cut leaf read from outside is never negated (proved by hand), so readings are 1 where every stored bit is 1. Across 43,091 networks in five frozen families, cuts and names read AND, OR, single bits and constants, never a negation (computed).

results.title: A handle grown at a knot sphere's line lets learning remove the dissonance the sphere forces
results.statement: Splicing a Fano atom at a line of a knot sphere makes a torus whose law extends with no even face, and if the grown law is its only unsatisfiable class, as computed on every grown torus from K_2 to K_5, learning at the dissonance with the state fixed then removes it. Every such removal changes a sign in the grown handle, so growth and learning together remove what neither removes alone.

results.title: Dissonance has a floor of half the Euler characteristic, so one grown handle is exactly enough
results.statement: In every state of every law on a knot space, violated lines plus over-agreement plus half the even faces is at least half the absolute Euler characteristic. So a sphere's dissonance cannot be resolved, one grown Fano atom reaches the torus's floor of zero, and every further atom adds a unit that no learning removes.

results.title: An acting atom with two sides held is a gate, and every map of held inputs is self-dual
results.statement: Flipping every point leaves the dissonance unchanged, so every map from held inputs is self-dual and none computes AND, OR or XOR of two inputs; an acting atom with two sides held is a gate (proved; exact). A learner seeing only its dissonance under the world's clamps learned gates at single atoms, NOT included, but not through composites (computed).

results.title: The leftover dissonance lives in whichever atom still acts as its line
results.statement: On every genus-2 space tested, with two Fano atoms grown into a knot sphere, the floor unit can sit only inside an atom that acts as its line or at its junctions, decided by SAT over every state. Which atom holds the leftover dissonance is therefore set by the law's class, what was learned, and not by the state.

results.title: In the layered memory, points apart move independently in every order, and floor units sit where the rule says
results.statement: In the two-level space no region holds three floor units and an acting composite holds exactly two, one per leaf (proved by hand, checked exactly). Disturbances in different composites learned away independently in every order with the address kept (320 of 320 pairs, computed), while points sharing a line interacted, mostly cancelling.
