results.title: Two readings of layers: a three-edge cut carries contradictions up, a parity name carries correlations
results.statement: Through a three-edge cut a lower level's unsatisfiable class becomes the upper level's constraint, so a dissonance crosses levels; through a parity name it cannot, and each level keeps its own (proved by hand). Names instead carry class-dependent correlations of the lower level's states, single clauses included, which no cut can offer (computed).

results.title: A uniform growth rule grows a remembering handle only with the Fano plane
results.statement: Splicing a lattice torus less a point at a violated line with one sign pattern on every line grows an atom that holds the dissonance exactly for the Fano torus with a constant pattern (proved by hand from the uniform-Fano theorem); every other class-forced atom grows transparent, and learning can then write it into its acting class.

results.title: A learner that sees only its own dissonance writes the layered memory exactly
results.statement: Told only the address and seeing only its own dissonance, a learner that tests its memory by letting its state wander and learns only where the answer is wrong wrote 100 of 100 frozen addresses exactly, each held (computed). An acting atom's dissonance can never be walked away (proved), so the test errs only by a false 1.

results.title: A group of atoms behind a three-edge cut is an atom of the next level, reading as the AND of its atoms
results.statement: A knot sphere with a flat state at every line, carrying atoms that each act in exactly one class and are free, is again such an atom: less any point it acts as its replaced line exactly where every atom inside acts, at any depth, and a composite of genus g holds g - 1 units, g where it acts (proved by hand). Computed: the AND at 274 removed points, 576 classes exact, 11 of 12 two-level addresses held.

results.title: Class-level readings of a learned knot memory are monotone; a negation needs a frame
results.statement: A reading that depends only on the stored classes, by any network whose other constraints leave the leaves' signs alone, is non-decreasing in every acting bit and cannot tell non-acting classes apart (proved by hand, by a gauge on the leaf's inner points). A negation exists only for one fixed signing per class, a frame learning's path decides (computed).

results.title: A torus atom remembers exactly where its torus has no satisfying state: the atom rule for every class-forced free torus atom on any host
results.statement: A torus atom grown on any orientable Kasteleyn knot space acts as its replaced line exactly where its torus has no satisfying state, transparent elsewhere, and holds a unit where it acts, whenever the torus is free at the removed point (proved by hand). Every lattice torus to 30 points is free (computed), so the Fano and thin-torus atoms of even index remember, the rest never do, and the memory does not need the Fano plane.

results.title: With a check that does not accept too soon, a learned knot memory learns every gate through composites from examples
results.statement: Making each negative check four longer walks, three from fresh states, removed every false acceptance in 156 writes at 2.5 times the probe's cost. With it a learner that keeps what its walk shows holding learned all 84 of its gate targets, through composites too, with no outside map (computed).

results.title: Maps of three held points in a knot memory are unate: no parity, no majority
results.statement: On every class of six spaces, no map of three held points at a group's interfaces is parity, majority or non-unate; the only total ones copy or negate one input (exact, with the frame lemma covering every law). A learner never accepted parity or majority (computed).

results.title: Learning from examples reaches knot memories three levels deep and three atoms wide
results.statement: A learner that sees only its own dissonance under the world's clamps learned and held every one of 40 gate writes at composites holding a leaf three levels down or three atoms, with no false stop (computed). Depth cost nothing; a second atom about eighteen times the steps; a third nothing more.

results.title: A learned knot memory computes the parity of three held points
results.statement: A learner that sees only its own dissonance learned the parity of three held points from eight examples, on a torus alone and grown inside a memory, and held it after disturbance in 20 of 20 runs (computed). It is the first learned map that is not unate.

results.title: One handle is enough: an eight-point torus counts three held points
results.statement: An eight-point lattice torus, in its most constrained class, forces a fourth point to the parity of any three held points (exact); sixteen of 281 lattice tori do. A planar disk gadget would make planar NAE-3SAT NP-hard, so one handle is the least, unless P equals NP.

results.title: An eight-point knot space of genus four computes the parity of three held points
results.statement: Hold three points of an eight-point knot space of genus four at any values and every floor state forces a fourth to their parity (exact, three independent readings). Small knot spaces compute majority often; the learned memories' interfaces stay unate, so their limit is their shape, not knot logic.
